TBP and BTF1B (TFIIB) can be recruited to SNAP-dependent Pol II and Pol III promoters, respectively, but TBP prevents BTF1B recruitment to Pol II, whereas BTF1B prevents TBP recruitment to Pol III.
TBP prevents BRF2 recruitment and promotes BRF2 recruitment at Pol II and Pol III promoters, respectively.
TBP both prevents BRF2 recruitment and enhances BRF2 recruitment, and that TBP recruitment is separate from TFIIs recruitment.

understanding the mechanisms by which cells control gene expression.
understanding how the cell regulates transcription of genes that encode small nuclear RNAs.
the molecular mechanism of transcriptional regulation in eukaryotic cells, with a particular focus on RNA polymerase III (Pol III).

the presence of a TBP-TFIIE-TFIIF-TFIIH complex at a promoter is the key factor in the determination of the polymerase that transcribes that promoter.
the TBP-TFIID complex, TFIIB, SNAPc, TFIIA, BRF2, and TBP-BRE complexes are the major players in this process.

the TATA box determines which of the two Pol II/III-specific general transcription factors, TFIIB or BRF2, can bind to SNAPc.
